title: Polenta con Ragù
subtitle: Soft polenta with slow-cooked beef ragù
excerpt: Creamy, buttery soft polenta topped with a rich beef ragù slow-cooked with red wine and tomatoes. A northern Italian staple, polenta replaces pasta as the vehicle for the sauce in Lombardy, Veneto, and Friuli.

recipe.sourceNotes: Polenta with ragù is a pillar of northern Italian cooking, particularly in the regions of Lombardy, Trentino-Alto Adige, Veneto, and Friuli-Venezia Giulia where polenta, not pasta, was historically the carbohydrate staple of the poor. The combination with a slow-cooked meat sauce dates to at least the eighteenth century, though the dish predates the introduction of tomatoes from the Americas.

content.text: Soft polenta must be stirred almost continuously during cooking and it takes between 40 and 50 minutes for traditional stone-ground polenta to lose its raw, gritty taste. Quick-cook polenta is ready in 5 minutes and perfectly good for a weeknight. Finish the polenta with plenty of butter and parmesan, it should taste like a rich side dish on its own before the ragù goes on top.

Make the ragù: heat the oil in a heavy pot. Cook the onion, carrot, and celery for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Increase heat and add the mince, breaking it up and browning for 8 minutes. Add the tomato puree and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine, reduce by half. Add the tomatoes, stock, and bay leaves. Season. Simmer, partially covered, for 1.5 hours until thick and rich.

Make the polenta: bring the stock to a boil with 1 teaspoon of salt. Pour in the polenta in a steady stream, whisking constantly. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, for 40 minutes (or as directed on the packet for quick-cook). The polenta should be thick and pull from the sides of the pan.

Off the heat, beat in the butter and parmesan. Taste for salt and pepper. The polenta should be creamy and rich, add a splash more stock if it has become too stiff. Spoon into warm bowls and top generously with the ragù.
